raw_segments.text: True, he replied, I'll redeem it at once.
Let me introduce the topic handle by mentioning that in London it is not the custom to put
the knife in the mouth, for fear of accidents, and that while the fork is reserved for that
use, it is not put further in the necessary.
It is scarcely worth mentioning, only it's as well to do as other people do.
Also, the spoon is not generally used overhand but under.
You get at your mouth better, which after all is the object, and you save a good deal
of the attitude of opening oysters on the part of the right elbow.
